title: Martial Arts Private Lesson Booking Software (2026)
description: Private lesson and appointment booking for martial arts schools: 10 tools compared on self-booking, pay at booking, lesson packs, instructor pay and price.
h1: Martial arts private lesson booking software
body:
Private lessons are often the highest-priced thing a martial arts school sells. A student books an hour with the head instructor before a belt test, a parent buys a 10-lesson pack, an adult wants 1:1 self-defense work. The software has to show each instructor's open times, let the student book (or let the front desk book for them), take payment or use up a lesson credit, remind everyone, and keep track of who taught what so instructors get paid correctly.

This page compares what ten vendors publish about private lesson and appointment booking. We checked each vendor's own pricing, feature and help pages on November 27, 2026. We haven't used these tools ourselves and we don't publish ratings. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. Prices are in US dollars. For group intro classes, see martial arts trial class booking software. If you teach privates without your own gym, see software for independent martial arts instructors.

What private lesson booking needs to do

  • Instructor calendars. Each instructor's own available hours, with gaps between lessons, so two students can't book the same slot.
  • Self-booking or staff booking. Some tools let students pick a time online. Others have staff set the appointment and email the student.
  • Payment that fits how you sell privates. Pay at booking, lesson packs, or credits that come with a membership.
  • Reminders. A missed private is an hour of an instructor's time with no one to teach.
  • Instructor tracking and pay. Which instructor taught which lesson, for payroll or commission.

Students booking themselves vs the front desk booking

Gymdesk, Zen Planner, MatPilot, RhinoFit and Spark describe students booking a private slot themselves, online or in the app. Spark goes furthest on payment: it says it collects payment when a student books a private lesson and assigns that lesson to a specific instructor. PushPress describes staff scheduling appointments, including recurring weekly or monthly sessions, from the dashboard or Staff App without the member buying credits first. Kicksite's help center describes appointments that staff create and attach to a student or prospect, who then gets an email. That fits schools where privates are arranged in person. Dojo Champ describes matching private lessons to instructor time slots and student preferences but doesn't say whether students book them online. Martialytics doesn't mention private lessons on the pages we checked, so ask during the 30-day trial.

Do extra instructors cost more?

For most martial arts tools here, no. Gymdesk lists unlimited staff accounts, PushPress lists unlimited staff on every plan, Martialytics lists unlimited users, Zen Planner says staff are never charged, Dojo Champ is one flat price, and RhinoFit Standard is a flat $57/mo. Kicksite and Spark don't publish user limits. Vagaro is the exception because it charges per bookable calendar. A school with three instructors teaching privates would pay $30 + $10 + $10 = $50/mo on Vagaro's list price ($23.99 base for the first 6 months), before card processing. Vagaro is a general booking app, so you'd still need something else for belt ranks and memberships.

Do private-only students count toward your bill?

Some families only buy privates. On tools priced by student count, that matters. Zen Planner counts anyone with a membership or who attended an event in the past month, but says pay-per-session attendees are never counted. Gymdesk doesn't count visitors, prospects, or frozen and cancelled members; ask whether a client who only has a lesson pack counts as a visitor. Martialytics and Kicksite price by active students and don't say how private-only students count. Dojo Champ and Spark have one price no matter how many students you have. PushPress charges per location, and MatPilot Pro has no per-member fee.

How to choose

  • You want students to book and pay up front: Spark (Paid Appointments, payment at booking, instructor earnings) describes the full flow. Zen Planner (online booking plus session packs and payroll) is the main alternative among tools that publish prices.
  • Privates are arranged in person and you just need them on the calendar: Kicksite's staff-set appointments or PushPress's recurring appointments cover this. PushPress has appointments on its $0 Free plan.
  • Small school on a tight budget: PushPress Free ($0, but 4.99% + $0.30 per card payment), RhinoFit Start Up ($0 at 20 or fewer active users) or MatPilot Free ($0 + 2%). Compare the fees in payment processing fees explained.
  • Paying instructors per lesson: look at Spark (tracks staff earnings), Zen Planner (payroll on every plan), PushPress (Payroll Report) and Dojo Champ (scheduling data feeds payroll). Ask each one to show you a per-private pay rate in the demo.

faq: Which martial arts software lets students book private lessons online?

Gymdesk (bookable time slots for private lessons), Spark Membership (Paid Appointments with real-time availability), Zen Planner (clients book 1-on-1 sessions online), MatPilot (one-on-one sessions on a public booking page) and RhinoFit (one-on-one sessions members schedule online or in the app) describe this on their own pages (checked 2026-11-27).
Can I take payment when a private lesson is booked?

Spark says its Paid Appointments feature collects payment at the time of booking and lets members use membership credits for appointments. Zen Planner sells session packs and custom packages, and MatPilot sells prepaid packs and pay links. The other vendors' pages don't say whether privates are paid at booking (checked 2026-11-27).
Which tools help pay instructors for private lessons?

Spark says you can assign staff to appointments and track their earnings. Zen Planner lists payroll management on every plan, PushPress lists a Payroll Report on every plan, and Dojo Champ says scheduling data can feed payroll systems for pay based on classes taught (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-27).
Is there free software for martial arts private lessons?

PushPress lists appointments on its $0 Free plan, with card processing at 4.99% + $0.30. RhinoFit's Start Up plan is $0 for 20 or fewer active users and includes Class & Appointment Scheduling, though it may restrict communications and payment processing. MatPilot Free is $0 plus a 2% platform fee and lists one-on-one sessions among its features, but doesn't say which features are on the Free plan (pricing pages, checked 2026-11-27).
Do I pay more for each instructor who teaches privates?

Not with most martial arts tools: Gymdesk, PushPress, Martialytics, Zen Planner, Dojo Champ and RhinoFit Standard don't charge per staff member. Vagaro charges $10/mo (US) for each extra bookable calendar, up to seven, on top of $30/mo for the first (pricing pages, checked 2026-11-27).
